## Overview

Apply the existing model-owned checkpoint selection hook to RunAI ModelStreamer before reading safetensors shards. Closes #60691; extends the DefaultModelLoader optimization in #60152 without duplicating MTP naming rules.

## Performance: Qwen3.5 MTP with remote RunAI

Five alternating baseline/patch pairs ran on the same H20×8 node (TP=8), with the same checkpoint, serving arguments, resources and experiment-only quantization compatibility setting. Both images shared the same runtime base; only the RunAI loader override differed. All ten replicas reached Kubernetes Ready with zero restarts. Each passed four fixed HTTP requests (256 output tokens total) with nonzero draft acceptance.

| Metric | Baseline median (range), 5 runs | Patch median (range), 5 runs | Median improvement |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Scheduled → Kubernetes Ready | 473 s (450–511) | 360 s (326–394) | 1.31×; 113 s less |
| Draft load and weight-finalization window | 143.646 s (135.974–147.128) | 14.908 s (14.444–15.724) | 9.64×; 128.738 s less |

The five paired observations, in execution order (baseline → patch, seconds), were:

- Scheduled → Ready: 473 → 360, 477 → 394, 462 → 379, 450 → 353, 511 → 326.
- Draft window: 143.646 → 14.572, 146.395 → 14.444, 141.378 → 15.724, 135.974 → 14.908, 147.128 → 15.054.

The median improvements are separately calculated statistics, not additive stage savings. The main-load window varied considerably and showed no stable improvement. Compilation, CUDA Graph capture, and warmup remained enabled and still contribute to Ready time.

RunAI checkpoint iterator entries for the draft fell from **75,881 to 1,121**; main remained at 75,881. The code path therefore ran, but entries are not measured object-store bytes, and the draft window includes more than pure I/O. Pending time is excluded. Pod events showed cached application images in every run. One patch run had a 58 s post-scheduling, pre-main interval, retained in the total. OSS/network load was not controlled, and no independent I/O/CPU bottleneck profile was taken; this is a result for this checkpoint and environment, not a general speedup guarantee.

Initial TP=8 runs had near-zero draft acceptance in **both** arms: this checkpoint's compressed-tensors ignore entry for mtp did not match its BF16 draft subtree under this runtime's exact-name matching. The reported pairs apply the same experiment-only subtree regex to **both** arms. That configuration change is not in this PR. Across restarts, some generated continuations differed even baseline versus baseline, so the fixed requests demonstrate working serving and nonzero draft use, not numerical equivalence or a full accuracy evaluation.

The final PR commit was separately rebuilt and checked on GPU: Ready, zero restarts, four HTTP 200 responses, 256 output tokens, and 122/133 draft tokens accepted/proposed. This one final-image check is not mixed into the five-pair performance medians. A local RunAI Qwen3.5 smoke test also reached Ready with nonzero draft acceptance. Exact OSS bytes were not measured.

## Additional GLM-5.3 MTP check (one pair, remote RunAI)

GLM-5.3 uses the existing DeepSeek-V3.2/GLM MTP model hook; this PR adds no GLM-specific naming rule. A separate H20×8, TP=8 baseline/patch pair used the same checkpoint, node, GPUs and serving configuration, changing only the loader image. Both replicas reached Ready with zero restarts and served four HTTP 200 requests (256 output tokens total per arm) with nonzero draft acceptance.

| Metric | Baseline | Patch |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Main RunAI iterator entries | 118,629 | 118,629 |
| Draft RunAI iterator entries | 118,629 | 2,698 |
| Scheduled → Kubernetes Ready | 1,735 s | 1,079 s |
| Draft load/weight-finalization window | 705.267 s | 21.896 s |

This is one paired observation, not a repeated performance estimate. Iterator entries are not measured OSS bytes; mixed shards can still be read in full. The GLM runtime disabled global torch.compile in both arms, although graph/kernel warmup still ran, so these figures do not establish compile-on performance. Exact object-store bytes were not measured.

## Design and implementation

- **Why before the iterator:** RunAI previously prepared the complete checkpoint file list before the model's load_weights method could discard unwanted MTP tensors. A later filter cannot undo whole-file RunAI reads. The loader now obtains the existing model-owned is_unused_checkpoint_weight predicate and selects complete shards before constructing the RunAI iterator. This PR does not define new MTP naming rules or add hooks to model classes; #60152 introduced the hook for opted-in models.
- **How selection works:** Local checkpoints reuse the safetensors-header selector. For S3-compatible and other remote storage, the loader reads model.safetensors.index.json at the resolved weights URI (including model_weights overrides) and maps wanted tensor names to files before RunAI reads payloads. Mixed and unindexed shards remain included. Before excluding an indexed shard, RunAI's metadata reader verifies its actual safetensors header using range reads. If the index omits a required tensor or the header cannot be verified, selection retains the original full list. Only selection metadata is fetched locally; weight payloads are not staged to disk.
- **Safety and distributed behavior:** Selection retains original file order. WORLD CPU ranks agree on a conservative union of required files; differing original file lists disable selection. With distributed RunAI and pipeline parallelism, selection retains the original full file list and skips the new WORLD agreement collective, preserving the existing streaming path. Without a model hook, or with missing/unusable optional index metadata, the original full file list is used. If the predicate rejects every shard, the full list is retained so the model's own missing-weight error can still surface. Model-rule and tensor-read errors propagate.
- **Scope and tradeoff:** This is file-level selection, not tensor-range filtering: a mixed shard is still read in full. The extra index fetch, header-range reads for excluded shards and CPU collective are the cost. Earlier Hugging Face checkpoint download and runai_streamer_sharded are unchanged. Examples of existing hook-bearing MTP implementations include Qwen3.5, Qwen3-Next, Nemotron-H and DeepSeek-V3.2/GLM; unadapted models keep the full-list fallback.

This complements #60152 (Default loader) and #58016 (lazy per-tensor reads): the former owns the model rule, while this PR applies it to RunAI whole-file loading. It also complements #48023/#42060 (draft weights URI inheritance).

## Tests and CI status

The review fixes add a runtime default checkpoint-selection method that keeps all weights, preserve detection of structural models without the optional hook, and add regressions for stale indexes and unavailable shard headers. The real Qwen3.5 MTP checkpoint E2E test is included. This follow-up passed local Ruff, formatting and Python syntax checks; the new native RunAI and GPU cases have not been executed in this follow-up and await the authorized upstream test run. The performance measurements above were not repeated for these review fixes.

Commit focused model-loader tests: **44 passed, 4 deselected**, including five real two-process Gloo selection/fallback cases. Separate RunAI/S3-emulator fixtures exercise actual file GETs and tensor values with Qwen3.5, Qwen3-Next and Nemotron-H predicates. Changed-file pre-commit, including mypy, passed locally. Full-repository pytest did **not** pass: CPU collection lacked soundfile. Upstream CI is **not green**: the pre-run authorization gate and Read the Docs build failed, while full Buildkite CI has not run. These are not represented as passing checks.

AI assistance was used to investigate, implement, test and prepare this change; the submitter reviewed the contents.

- [x] **Testing and Validation:** Reports tested paths, sample counts, and limits; CI constraints are explicit.
- [x] **Code Quality and Style:** Keeps code and comments clear and updates relevant documentation and examples.
- [x] **Pull Request Contents:** Includes a summary, links, measured data, root cause, trade-offs, and limitations.

+## Model-specific checkpoint selection
+
+For models exposing `is_unused_checkpoint_weight`, `runai_streamer` skips
+safetensors files containing only unused weights before streaming. It uses the
+same model-owned rule as the default loader, including MTP draft models with
+this hook; it does not assume a particular MTP tensor prefix.
+
+Object-storage checkpoints use `model.safetensors.index.json` and verify excluded
+shards against their safetensors headers before streaming. Mixed shards remain
+included. Missing or inconsistent metadata retains the original file list.
+Models without a selection rule keep all files. Distributed streaming with
+pipeline parallelism also retains the full file list. This optimization does
+not change `runai_streamer_sharded`.
+
 ## Tunable parameters
 
 You can tune parameters using `--model-loader-extra-config`:

🔴 With distributed RunAI streaming, pipeline parallelism and a draft model, startup can hang while loading the drafter. Base never ran a world-wide collective here. The new `all_gather_object` uses `get_world_group()`, which every world rank must join. The drafter is only built on the last PP rank (gpu_model_runner.py:603), so ranks on other stages never call it. Fix: run the agreement only on the ranks that load this model, e.g. the group RunAI's distributed streamer itself uses. Also skip it when `is_unused_weight` is None, so models without the hook avoid the extra collective.

<details>
<summary>Why this was flagged</summary>

Trigger: `--model-loader-extra-config '{"distributed": true}'` with `--load-format runai_streamer`, pipeline_parallel_size > 1 and speculative decoding that loads a draft model. In vllm/v1/worker/gpu_model_runner.py:603 the drafter is only created when `get_pp_group().is_last_rank`, so `self.drafter.load_model` (line 5255) runs on last-stage ranks only. Each of those ranks reaches `_get_weights_iterator`, where runai_streamer_loader.py:209-213 calls `torch.distributed.all_gather_object` on `get_world_group().cpu_group`. That group includes every PP stage. Ranks on other stages never enter the call, so the last-stage ranks block until the process-group timeout and the server fails to start. On the base branch this function ran no world collective. The collective also runs when the model has no `is_unused_checkpoint_weight` hook, so drafters without the hook are affected too. One part is unverified from this checkout: whether RunAI's own distributed streaming already spans the whole world group in this setup.

🟡 (optional) Users of object-storage MTP checkpoints with a stale index can get a draft model with silently unloaded weights, which the base branch never produces. Remote selection drops a shard because the index `weight_map` says it holds only unused tensors. It never checks what the shard actually contains. The RunAI `load_weights` (line 244) does not check for missing weights, so nothing raises. Fix: never drop a shard based only on index entries. Read each candidate shard's safetensors header (the remote analogue of the local selector), or fall back to the full list unless every wanted tensor maps to a kept shard.

<details>
<summary>Why this was flagged</summary>

The trigger is an object-storage checkpoint whose `model.safetensors.index.json` is out of date. For example, MTP or draft tensors were added to an existing shard without updating the index. The comment at line 80 says such older indexes exist. They are only covered when the draft tensors sit in separate unindexed files. For a shard listed in the index whose indexed names all satisfy `is_unused_weight`, the shard lands in `indexed` but not in `needed`, so line 82 drops it. Its real contents are never read. On the base branch every listed file is streamed. After this change the drafter's tensors never reach `load_weights`. `RunaiModelStreamerLoader.load_weights` (line 242-244) and the MTP `load_weights` methods do not verify that all weights loaded, so the draft runs with uninitialized weights instead of failing. The `kept or files` fallback only applies when every shard is dropped.

**Verification:** Verification: `_filter_remote_weights` keeps `[path for path in files if path not in indexed or path in needed]`. Nothing ever opens the shard's own safetensors header. `RunaiModelStreamerLoader.load_weights` (line 244) just calls `model.load_weights(...)`. The drafter runs with uninitialized MTP weights. On base, RunAI streamed every file from `list_safetensors`, so this checkpoint loaded fully.

</details>
